title: Slatelet batching primer & rough PRD
content:
Context:

Quick notes on an experiment idea that keeps coming up in calls: group very short LLM requests (1–30 tokens of model output expected) into tiny bundles I’m calling "slatelets" to reduce per-request overheads and increase GPU utilization without blowing up tail latency. This is a working primer / rough PRD — half brainstorming, half implementation checklist.

Problem we’re solving:
- Many customers (chat UIs, assistant microtasks, auto-summaries, autocomplete) make a large number of short, low-latency requests.
- Per-request fixed costs (kernel launch, RPC, prefix processing, KV handling, trace/provenance) dominate cost and block throughput.
- Naive batching increases average latency and can violate p95 SLOs.

Hypothesis:
If we identify short-response requests and batch them into slatelets with a short wait window (e.g., 5–15 ms) and use a prioritized tiny-batch execution path, we can:
1) Reduce per-request unit cost by 20–50% for these flows.
2) Preserve p95/p99 latency within SLO by bounding hold-time and offering fast-path execution.
3) Improve GPU kernel utilization for short sequences.

Design sketch / concepts:
- Slatelet: a logical group of 2–32 short requests that share a scheduling window. Slatelets are independent (no cross-request context).
- Detection: annotate request at ingestion with a "slatelet_hint" or auto-detect from historical token distributions and route.
- Hold window: small configurable delay (default 8ms) to collect co-arrivals. Timeout ensures single-request progress.
- Priority lanes: requests can opt into "latency-sensitive" (min hold) or "cost-sensitive" (longer hold, more batching).
- Execution path: micro-batches use specialized kernel dispatch optimized for short sequences and concurrent KV cache handling.
- Response demux: map outputs to originating request IDs and stream partial tokens back if needed.

API considerations:
- New opt-in request field: slatelet_hint: { "latency_priority": "high|low", "expected_tokens": int } OR server-side auto: slatelet_strategy: auto/strict/off.
- Telemetry: expose per-request metadata about batching latency, batch size, kernel type.
- SDK: convenience wrapper to mark small-generation calls (e.g., streaming autocomplete).

User stories (rough):
- As a front-end engineer, I want autocompletes to be cheap and fast, so I can send many quick prompt completions without spiky bills.
- As an ML platform engineer, I want telemetry showing how slatelet batches behaved (avg size, hold-time, failure rate) so I can tune rollout.
- As ops, I want a fallback (no-batch) toggle in console per-customer to avoid exposing risky behavior during early rollout.

Acceptance criteria (initial experiment):
- Cost: mean cost per 1k short-requests reduced by >=25% in the experiment cohort.
- Latency: p95 end-to-end latency increase <= +10ms compared to baseline for latency-priority requests.
- Correctness: 100% of requests return matching outputs; streaming clients receive stable token sequences in order.
- Observability: tracking dashboard (per model) for slatelet rate, avg batch size, hold-time distribution.

Implementation notes / technical risks:
- Demuxing streaming tokens: careful about partial token emission when requests in the same batch finish at different token lengths; need per-request streaming boundaries.
- Prefix/KV caching: merging requests with different prefixes can be expensive; restrict slatelets to same-prefix or use prefix-hash binning.
- Memory pressure: batch size spikes could increase KV cache usage (need soft cap).
- Tail latency: conservative hold-window and immediate fallback (execute single request if queueing exceeds threshold).
- Side effects on QoE: batched execution could shift sampling randomness/noise; ensure seed isolation per request.

Experiment plan (MVP):
1) Simulation run on production traces (offline) to estimate arrival coalescing and ideal hold window. Owner: Mika. Due: 11/15.
2) Prototype in serving runtime: implement in queuing layer, minimal kernel path for 1–8 token batches, demux logic. Owner: Arjun. Branch: srv/slatelet-mvp.
3) Canary: route 1% of traffic from customers with many short requests (autocomplete) to slatelet path. Measure cost, p95, errors for 2 weeks.
4) Dashboard and kill-switch in console.

Metrics to collect:
- avg_slatelet_size, slatelet_hold_ms, percent_requests_in_slatelets, cost_per_request, p95_latency, p99_latency, token_loss_rate, streaming_consistency_violations.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we require same model & same model args to batch? (prob yes).
- How do we handle tool-calling/function calls inside slatelets? likely disallow initial rollout.
- SLA language update: need to document that some minor additional wait may be introduced for cost-sensitive lanes.
- UX: SDK convenience vs implicit auto-detect (which may surprise users).

Next steps (short):
- Run offline trace sim (Mika) to propose default hold window and batch size cap.
- Draft small prototyping checklist for Arjun: queuing hook, demux, per-request timer, metrics.
- Put a short note in product backlog (JIRA-1128) linking this doc and simulation results.

Notes to self:
- Keep early rollout opt-in and customer-visible.
- Avoid mixing long-history prefix requests with slatelets.
- Think about combining with prefix cache hits — if many requests share KV hit, batching might be even cheaper.

Slack refs: #serving-runtime, #console-ops.

Rough timeline: proto (2 sprints) -> canary (2 weeks) -> expand to 10% (1–2 weeks) if metrics good.

End of primer.
